paras: The Monaghan mills shooting was the pursuit and shooting of Bill Thompson, a Black laborer, by a group of white men at the Monaghan cotton mill construction site outside Greenville, South Carolina, on the morning of 14 August 1900. Thompson was shot in the jaw but survived, and nearly all the Black laborers on the job quit work. White papers reported it as a 'race riot', while a Black correspondent described a strike provoked by the white foreman.

The Flint Building and Construction Company, whose superintendent was A. F. McNally, was building the Monaghan mills about two miles from Greenville with about fifty white and nearly 200 Black workmen.

According to the white accounts, McNally separated Thompson and another Black worker who were fighting, and Thompson cursed him. Ordered off the premises, Thompson was said to have thrown a rock, four or five pounds by the Greenville News's estimate, that struck McNally's arm. When he ran, about half a dozen white men chased him and fired several shots, one lodging in his neck; the dispatch said he was 'not seriously hurt'.

The Black laborers then quit work, and the Greenville News said they armed themselves with hatchets, axes, rocks and pistols before things quieted down. No report of an arrest, a charge against Thompson or any action against the men who fired was found.

The Americus Times-Recorder ran the Greenville dispatch on 16 August under 'RACE RIOT AT GREENVILLE' and 'Negro Precipitates a Difficulty'. The Newberry Herald and News reprinted the Greenville News on 17 August under headlines praising 'sensible white men' and denouncing a 'Brutal Attack on Superintendent McNalley by Furious Negroes'.

The only Black-press report found, a Greenville item in the Plaindealer on 31 August, told the story as a strike of 'over two hundred colored men'. It named no worker and made McNally the aggressor, with white men arriving 'with sticks and guns'.

The white papers said Thompson cursed McNally and threw a rock at him, while the Plaindealer said McNally cursed a worker who told him it was 'no white man's business', struck him first, and was thrashed. Only the Greenville dispatch said Black workers also fired; the Plaindealer said the man was shot at four times.

reader.title: Monaghan mills shooting
bases: A group of white men (white bosses, 'a half dozen white men') pursued a Black laborer and shot him in the jaw at a mill construction site, without killing him (A3, A4, A7).

A Greenville dispatch (A3), the Greenville News (A4) and a Black-press correspondent (A7) agree that a Black worker at the Monaghan mills was pursued by white men and shot in the jaw after a clash with McNally, though they differ on who struck first.

accounts.label: Greenville dispatch
accounts.gist: After Thompson fought another Black laborer and cursed the superintendent who parted them, he threw a rock that hit the superintendent's arm; white bosses chased him and shots were fired by both sides, Thompson being shot in the neck but not seriously hurt.

accounts.label: Greenville News
accounts.gist: Thompson 'made an attack' on McNally and hurled a four-to-five-pound rock that would have killed him; a half dozen white men pursued and shot him in the jaw, and nearly 200 armed Black workers were kept from 'any overt act' by the whites' 'splendid judgment'.

accounts.label: Black correspondent (Plaindealer)
accounts.gist: Two workers settled a dispute; foreman McNally cursed one, was told it was 'no white man's business', struck him and was thrashed; white men came with sticks and guns and shot at the fleeing man four times, and over 200 Black workers struck.

framing.detail: Headlined 'RACE RIOT AT GREENVILLE' with 'Negro Precipitates a Difficulty', blaming Thompson and noting 'the negroes being better armed than the whites'.

Greenville News headlines 'A RACE RIOT AVERTED ... BY SENSIBLE WHITE MEN' and 'Brutal Attack on Superintendent McNalley by Furious Negroes', praising the white men and calling Thompson 'without doubt in the wrong'.
A local-news brief framed it as a strike, with the white foreman cursing and striking first and white men arriving 'with sticks and guns'.
